subject: APAC demo — clarify cross-day invite behavior for JST / SGT / AEST

To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 09:34:00 +0900
Subject: Re: Redwood demo — timezone on invite

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for the invite — quick question. The calendar event we received is labeled "Dec 17, 23:30" (UTC) and shows up in our Tokyo calendar as "Dec 18, 08:30" but the subject line still says Dec 17. A few of our folks are worried they might miss it if the label says the previous day.

Can you confirm the intended local time for Tokyo / Singapore / Sydney attendees? Also, will the invite include an explicit timezone tag (e.g., JST / SGT / AEST) so local folks don't get the "next-day" shock?

Appreciate it — Kenji

--
Kenji Sato
Head of Platform Integrations
Hikari HealthTech
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.inference>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.inference>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 10:05:00 +0900
Subject: Re: Redwood demo — timezone on invite

Hi Kenji — thanks for flagging, and sorry for the confusion.

Short answer: the demo was scheduled for 08:30 JST / 07:30 SGT / 09:30 AEST on Dec 18 (local times). The invite was created from our US-based booking system using UTC date-times, which resulted in the event title showing Dec 17 in UTC. The calendar itself converts to local times for recipients, but the title and reminder text sometimes retain the creator's date label, which is what's causing the worry.

I've attached a corrected .ics (hikari-demo-ics.ics) that explicitly lists the local start times and includes the timezone strings in the summary. I'm also looping in Marcus (AE) to confirm whether you prefer we send an updated invite or just a clarification note + local-time event. Mina from CS is on the thread to own the onboarding checklist once we lock the slot.

Proposed options:
- Option A: Send updated invite with local-time summary and calendar description including both JST / SGT / AEST and UTC.
- Option B: Keep the existing invite but send a short confirmation email with the explicit local-time table and a calendar quick-link.

Which do you prefer? If you confirm, we'll push the updated invite and include a short note to all participants so nobody is surprised by the date label.

Thanks — Sofia
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference

Kenji — quick one from me. Option A is cleaner for customer-facing scheduling: updated invite that contains clear local labels and a short line in the description: "Local times shown: JST (UTC+9) | SGT (UTC+8) | AEST (UTC+10). Please rely on your calendar's local time view."

Internally I'll also open a small ops ticket to add a one-line booking rule so our system sets the event title to the local date for the primary timezone of the attendee list. Sofia / Mina: can you add this as a note to the handoff-playbook.pdf in the onboarding folder?

Marcus
